candidates.name: FILE_ALLOCATED_RANGE_BUFFER
verified_facts: Defines offset and length pairs used to request and return allocated file ranges.
semantic_limits: Range arithmetic requires overflow, ordering, overlap, bounds, and file-size validation.

candidates.name: FSCTL_GET_COMPRESSION
verified_facts: Retrieves the current per-stream compression state for a file or directory.
semantic_limits: Compression state depends on file-system support and does not prove content equality or stability.

candidates.name: Compression State
verified_facts: Defines file and directory compression state and the read-only query contract.
semantic_limits: Compression state can inherit or change and must not be treated as a content or owner signature.

candidates.name: FSCTL_GET_INTEGRITY_INFORMATION
verified_facts: Retrieves integrity-stream configuration for a file or directory on supported file systems.
semantic_limits: Integrity configuration is not a successful scrub result, content hash, or receipt-validity proof.

candidates.name: FSCTL_GET_INTEGRITY_INFORMATION_BUFFER
verified_facts: Carries checksum algorithm, flags, and cluster-size fields returned by the integrity query.
semantic_limits: Returned fields require version, size, file-system, and handle validation before use.

candidates.name: FSCTL_GET_OBJECT_ID
verified_facts: Retrieves an existing NTFS object identifier without creating a new one.
semantic_limits: Object IDs can be absent and are not content hashes, stable cross-volume identities, or owner proof.

candidates.name: FILE_OBJECTID_BUFFER
verified_facts: Carries an object ID plus birth-volume, birth-object, and domain identifiers.
semantic_limits: Object-identifier fields must be treated as metadata; modifying them is prohibited and can be destructive.

candidates.name: Distributed Link Tracking and Object Identifiers
verified_facts: Explains how NTFS object identifiers support distributed link tracking across moves.
semantic_limits: Link tracking is not guaranteed across all moves, versions, volumes, or disabled-service conditions.

candidates.name: FSCTL_GET_NTFS_VOLUME_DATA
verified_facts: Returns NTFS volume geometry and file-record sizing needed for subsequent NTFS queries.
semantic_limits: NTFS volume data is local structural metadata and does not prove a file belongs to the canonical task.

candidates.name: NTFS_VOLUME_DATA_BUFFER
verified_facts: Carries NTFS serial, sector, cluster, MFT, and file-record geometry.
semantic_limits: Values are volume-level snapshots and must be checked for bounds, version, and device continuity.

candidates.name: FSCTL_GET_NTFS_FILE_RECORD
verified_facts: Retrieves an NTFS file record at or below a requested file-reference number.
semantic_limits: The returned record may not match the requested number exactly and requires explicit reference validation.

candidates.name: NTFS_FILE_RECORD_INPUT_BUFFER
verified_facts: Carries the file-reference number requested by FSCTL_GET_NTFS_FILE_RECORD.
semantic_limits: A requested reference is not evidence that the returned record is the target without output correlation.

candidates.name: NTFS_FILE_RECORD_OUTPUT_BUFFER
verified_facts: Carries the returned reference, record length, and raw file-record bytes.
semantic_limits: Raw file-record parsing is version-sensitive and must not replace supported handle and file-ID checks.

candidates.name: FSCTL_GET_RETRIEVAL_POINTERS
verified_facts: Returns mappings from virtual cluster numbers to logical cluster extents for a file or stream.
semantic_limits: Extent maps are physical-layout snapshots and do not prove logical byte content or stable placement.

candidates.name: RETRIEVAL_POINTERS_BUFFER
verified_facts: Carries extent count, starting VCN, and VCN-to-LCN mappings.
semantic_limits: The first returned VCN can be rounded and sparse or partially allocated extents require special handling.

candidates.name: STARTING_VCN_INPUT_BUFFER
verified_facts: Specifies the virtual cluster number at which extent enumeration begins.
semantic_limits: Input VCN arithmetic must be bounded and resumed from returned NextVcn after buffer overflow.
